frameworks.name: Commercial Model Option Appraisal
frameworks.definition: A structured advisory method for comparing contracting models by aligning risk allocation, capability requirements, economics, and strategic fit before selecting the preferred commercial structure.
steps: Define the business objective and decision scope.
List the candidate commercial models to be compared.
Compare each model’s risk allocation, required capabilities, and operational implications.
Assess financial upside, downside, and implementation complexity.
Apply decision criteria and weight them against the sponsor’s priorities.
Select the model with the best overall strategic trade-off and test it against key sensitivities.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a sponsor is choosing between alternative contracting structures for a project or portfolio and needs a defensible recommendation.
failure_modes: Over-focusing on headline price while ignoring lifecycle risk and capability burden.
Treating all models as interchangeable despite very different governance requirements.
Using vague criteria that cannot support a decision with senior stakeholders.

frameworks.name: Natural Small-Room Concert Capture
frameworks.definition: A practical method for recording an acoustic ensemble in a live room while preserving a natural audience-like balance and minimizing amplification.
steps: Place musicians in a semi-circle so they can hear each other acoustically.
Use minimal close-miking and rely on room/overhead microphones for ensemble blend.
Keep vocal mics close to the mouth and monitors as quiet as possible.
Use the mixer to create a balanced stereo mix for recording.
Tame excessive room reflections with furniture, rugs, or blankets if needed.
frameworks.when_to_use: When recording an unplugged or lightly amplified acoustic ensemble in a small live room with limited gear.
failure_modes: Too much close-miking makes the recording sound unnatural.
Monitor volume is too high, causing feedback and masking acoustic instruments.
The room is too reflective, making the recording harsh or muddy.

If needed, use a second loudspeaker for room reinforcement at moderate volume.
Set gains conservatively and avoid clipping or feedback.

frameworks.name: Treatment-evidence ladder for hidradenitis suppurativa
frameworks.definition: A practical way to separate established HS therapies from emerging options by matching mechanism, trial maturity, and regulatory status.
steps: Start with therapies that have phase III evidence and regulatory approval for moderate-to-severe HS.
Separate off-label biologics and small molecules with only early-phase or mixed evidence.
Prioritize options by expected benefit, evidence strength, and patient suitability.
Treat experimental options as discussion points for specialist referral or clinical trials.
frameworks.when_to_use: When briefing a patient or clinician on the state of HS treatment options and how confident to be in each.
failure_modes: Confusing promising early data with proven standard care.
Overstating off-label therapies as established treatments.
Ignoring regulatory status and evidence maturity.

frameworks.name: Quality-of-life-first HS counseling lens
frameworks.definition: A patient-centered advisory lens that weighs symptom control, pain, function, and treatment burden alongside disease suppression.
steps: Clarify the patient’s main burdens: pain, flares, drainage, scarring, embarrassment, and mobility limits.
Match treatment intensity to the severity of quality-of-life impact, not only lesion count.
Discuss treatment trade-offs: onset of action, durability, adverse effects, and monitoring burden.
Revisit goals regularly because HS control and pain experience can change over time.
frameworks.when_to_use: When helping a patient make decisions about HS management beyond purely dermatologic endpoints.
failure_modes: Focusing only on lesion reduction and overlooking pain or psychosocial burden.
Underestimating the burden of long-term or injectable therapies.
Failing to align treatment choice with the patient’s lived priorities.

frameworks.name: Two-Dimension Prioritisation Lens for RRAM Interventions
frameworks.definition: A decision lens that screens candidate interventions by combining problem criticality, system-level resilience impact, and institutional readiness so scarce TA resources are directed where they can produce the most strategic effect.
steps: Start from a long list of candidate interventions grouped by theme and contract component.
Assess each candidate against a small set of criteria covering urgency, system-level impact, data/institutional readiness, and feasibility for SSATP-led support.
Use stakeholder consultation, including the AGM, to validate criteria and test whether local champions exist to carry the work forward.
Rank interventions by overall strategic fit rather than by technical appeal alone.
Select a balanced portfolio of knowledge products, capacity development, and pilots that can be delivered within the contract’s policy-oriented mandate.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a TA contract must choose among many dispersed infrastructure-resilience ideas and needs a transparent way to prioritise a manageable portfolio.
failure_modes: Treating the exercise as a generic scoring table without strategic judgement.
Overweighting asset-level fixes and underweighting system-level resilience gains.
Selecting interventions without checking whether stakeholders and champions exist to sustain them.
Assuming high-quality data and mature digital systems where the institutional reality is weak.

frameworks.name: Champion-Validated Portfolio Selection
frameworks.definition: A consultation-driven method that uses workshops and formal convenings to identify, test, and confirm in-country leaders or champions who can partner with SSATP and the TA contractor on specific interventions.
steps: Map potential country and institutional champions during stocktaking and early consultations.
Use the AGM or similar forums to scout, compare, and vet those champions against intervention needs.
Check whether the champion has convening power, reform credibility, and enough ownership to sustain follow-up.
Assign priority to interventions where a credible champion can mobilise action beyond the TA team.
Document where no champion exists and treat those areas as lower-priority or preparatory work for later phases.
frameworks.when_to_use: When success depends not only on technical merit but also on political and institutional sponsorship inside beneficiary countries or agencies.
failure_modes: Confusing enthusiasm with actual reform capacity.
Choosing countries or interventions without local ownership.
Treating the AGM as a formality rather than a real validation and scouting exercise.
Ignoring weak institutional incentives that can derail implementation.

playbooks.title: Build a Long-List-to-Priority Funnel for an Inception Report
playbooks.trigger: Use when an inception report must turn a broad catalogue of possible interventions into a concise, defensible prioritisation approach.

Present the screening criteria in a way that links diagnostics, institutional readiness, data availability, and expected system-level value.
Describe how the AGM will be used to validate assumptions, surface champions, and sharpen the shortlist.
End with a practical route from screening to implementation planning and portfolio shaping.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for advisory teams writing inception reports that must show rigour without pretending the intervention menu is already fixed.

frameworks.name: Triple-party concession handover protection
frameworks.definition: A legal-risk workflow for a public owner balancing transfer to a new concessionaire, legacy occupant claims, and municipal asset protection before signature.
steps: Inventory the asset package and identify legal, physical, and environmental gaps
Separate issues attributable to legacy occupation from those to be assumed by the new operator
Require documentary evidence, inspections, and defect mapping before formal handover
Allocate responsibility in the contract and closing documents for repairs, remediation, and latent defects
Preserve municipal recourse against the prior operator where rights or liabilities may still exist
frameworks.when_to_use: When a public authority must transition an asset from a legacy operator to a new concessionaire and needs to limit exposure to hidden defects or contamination.
failure_modes: Treating all pre-existing defects as automatically transferable to the new concessionaire

Failing to reserve claims against the outgoing operator
Ignoring environmental liabilities until after execution

playbooks.title: Concession viability and risk review for a fuel-site tender
playbooks.trigger: You need to assess whether a fuel-station concession is economically viable and legally coherent from the perspective of a public client or bidder.
steps: Read the tender conditions as an integrated package: scope, term, investment burden, operating obligations, and handover terms
Stress-test legal coherence: technical specifications, asset description, defects allocation, and environmental responsibilities
Estimate commercial viability using gross margin, volumes, capex, opex, and required return
Test downside scenarios for contamination, latent defects, and legacy occupancy issues
Translate findings into negotiating positions, bid cautions, or council recommendations

frameworks.name: Discord RAG App Decomposition
frameworks.definition: A modular way to separate message sync, embedding/indexing, retrieval, and user interaction for an AI assistant over Discord archives.
steps: Sync Discord messages into a local archive.
Build embeddings and a searchable index from the archive.
Retrieve the most relevant messages for a user query.
Generate an answer grounded in retrieved context.
Optionally render the response in JSON for downstream use.
frameworks.when_to_use: When turning a static message archive into an interactive question-answering tool.
failure_modes: Conflating retrieval and generation so answers are not grounded.
Treating sync, indexing, and UI as one script, making maintenance difficult.
Letting the app answer from stale data without update checks.

Create embeddings for message content and store them in a local vector index.
Use the retrieved messages as context for the LLM answer.
Offer a plain-language answer by default, with an optional JSON response mode.
Add a Streamlit interface for querying, viewing history, and rerunning the pipeline.

frameworks.name: LTWAF Project-Selection Lensing Framework
frameworks.definition: A four-lens method for comparing water importation concepts by source, deliverability, permitting complexity, and bankability before committing proposal effort.
steps: Classify each concept by water source and delivery geometry.
Test whether the concept can credibly deliver 10,000+ acre-feet per year with long-duration availability.
Screen major constraints: technical feasibility, environmental/regulatory burden, and cross-border or multi-jurisdiction complexity.
Compare likely financing pathways against risk allocation and payment realism.
Rank concepts by strategic fit, resilience, and probability of implementable approval.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when a client faces multiple heterogeneous water-supply concepts and needs a board-level basis for selecting which ones deserve proposal investment.
failure_modes: Treating all concepts as equally mature or equally financeable.
Ignoring permitting and cross-jurisdictional friction until late stage.
Overweighting headline supply volume while underweighting delivery and legal viability.

frameworks.name: Financing-and-Delivery Fit Matrix
frameworks.definition: A decision framework that matches each project's risk profile and revenue logic to the most plausible delivery model and financing structure.
steps: Map which party can best bear design, construction, operating, demand, permitting, and political risks.
Identify the payment mechanism available: availability-style payments, volumetric water sales, public subsidy, blended finance, or hybrid structures.
Check whether the project has a stable offtake or depends on long-term public support.
Stress-test the model against capex intensity, opex sensitivity, and stakeholder acceptance.
Select the structure that best aligns incentives, bankability, and implementation speed.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when evaluating whether a project should be proposed as a PPP, public-led program, hybrid financing, or another delivery form.
failure_modes: Assuming private finance is optimal for all large infrastructure.
Selecting a delivery model before understanding risk allocation.
Confusing technical desirability with financeability.

Identify where the firm can add value and where specialist partners are needed.
Frame the opportunity in terms of strategic fit, risk, and likely engagement duration.

playbooks.title: Build a Financing Strategy for a Multi-Concept Water Portfolio

steps: Group projects by capital intensity, regulatory burden, and revenue profile.
Assign candidate funding sources to each group, from public grants to project debt and blended structures.
Flag concepts that may need local delivery, exchange value, or political cross-subsidy to become viable.
Compare a single large-anchor project versus a portfolio strategy with complementary projects.
Prepare a financing narrative that explains why the mix improves resilience and bankability.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when the proposal includes a portfolio of water projects rather than a single asset or single technology.

frameworks.name: Phased Agent Modernisation Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A staged approach to evolve an AI analytics agent from MVP to a more accurate, maintainable, and proactive advisory system.
steps: Stabilise the ingestion, embedding, and retrieval pipeline before adding new features.
Add structured metadata filtering so answers can be constrained by channel, author, and time.
Introduce conversational memory and configuration management.
Layer in higher-order analytics such as trends, sentiment, graphs, and personalisation.
Add proactive scheduled outputs, alerts, and audit logging.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an AI agent has working basics but needs a roadmap to improve reliability, usefulness, and operational maturity.
failure_modes: Trying to add advanced features before the retrieval layer is stable.
Treating the roadmap as a one-time implementation plan rather than an iterative maturity path.
Ignoring metadata and governance until later, which reduces answer quality and traceability.

steps: Define the next step and its objective clearly.
Implement or validate that step before moving on.
Test the result against a realistic user question or workflow.
Capture errors, gaps, and refinements.
Proceed to the next step only after the current one is understood and accepted.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for advisory-style buildouts where the user wants controlled progress, frequent questions, and no leapfrogging across phases.

frameworks.name: Start-simple resource repository rollout
frameworks.definition: A staged advisory method for launching a resource library by starting with the simplest durable storage, then adding automation, search, and intelligence only after the core workflow proves useful.
steps: Choose a minimal repository format that the team can maintain easily.
Capture detected resources with essential metadata only at first.
Validate that the repository can be populated reliably from existing messages.
Add search, filtering, and tagging once the basic capture flow is stable.
Only then consider recommender or digest features.
frameworks.when_to_use: When launching a new knowledge repository or beta feature where reliability and adoption matter more than advanced automation.
failure_modes: Trying to build the full intelligence layer before the capture pipeline works.
Using a repository format that is too complex for non-technical maintainers.
Skipping the validation stage and accumulating low-quality data.

frameworks.name: Hybrid detection and classification pipeline
frameworks.definition: A decision framework that combines deterministic extraction methods with optional AI assistance, using AI only where it materially improves tagging or interpretation.
steps: Use regex or structured parsing to detect links, files, and obvious resource markers.
Extract metadata such as author, channel, timestamp, and nearby context.
Apply lightweight rule-based tags first when patterns are clear.
Escalate ambiguous cases to an AI classifier only if needed.
Store results in a structured repository for later search and review.
frameworks.when_to_use: When the use case includes both obvious structured signals and some ambiguous categories that may benefit from AI.
failure_modes: Using AI for every record when simple rules would suffice.
Overcomplicating the first version with multiple intelligence layers.
Creating inconsistent tags because rules and AI outputs are not governed.

playbooks.title: Launch a Markdown-first resource library
playbooks.trigger: You want an open-source, human-readable repository for collected resources that can later be hosted online.
steps: Pick a Markdown-first repository structure that is easy to browse and edit.
Store each resource as a separate Markdown file with consistent front matter or metadata.
Organize the files by topic, channel, or tag so they are easy to navigate.
If needed, publish the same content through a simple static site or wiki layer.
Keep the structure simple enough that non-programmers can review and maintain it.
playbooks.applicable_when: Best when the priority is durability, portability, and easy human review rather than a complex application backend.

playbooks.title: Validate a beta resource-detection feature in stages
playbooks.trigger: You need to implement a new content-detection workflow without overbuilding the first version.
steps: Start by detecting only the most obvious resources such as links and attachments.
Confirm that noise such as reactions or bot messages is excluded.
Check that metadata capture works before adding richer tagging.
Introduce intelligent tagging only after the basic extraction is reliable.
Expand to search, sorting, and recommendation features after the repository is populated.

playbooks.title: Phase-by-phase upgrade roadmap for a Discord AI agent with AI coding assistants
playbooks.trigger: When a non-programmer is using Copilot or similar tools to improve a prototype Discord bot and wants a safe implementation plan.
steps: Create a versioned repository and work in small branches so changes are reversible.
Define quality gates before changing logic: test each new feature and review AI-generated code carefully.
Move message storage toward an ID-first schema so guilds, channels, and messages are keyed by stable IDs rather than names.
Validate incoming Discord payloads against a typed model before storing or processing them.
Refactor ingestion so new messages are upserted idempotently and older JSON data is migrated into the same structure.
Add explicit channel and guild filters to search and summarization flows so the agent can scope results correctly.
Centralize jump URL creation in one place and ensure it always uses numeric guild, channel, and message IDs.
Break multifunction requests into a structured workflow: parse time range, filter messages, then summarize.
Add logging and tests around time parsing, filtering, and tool invocation so failures are visible instead of silent.
Use cloud deployment only after the local workflow is stable and the data model is consistent.

frameworks.name: Escalated MVP delivery for AI-enabled community analytics
frameworks.definition: A phased delivery method that starts with a proven minimal product focused on the highest-value use cases, then adds adjacent capabilities only after validating earlier stages.
steps: Identify the primary use cases and define the first usable version.
Sequence implementation into subphases that each add one coherent capability.
Validate each subphase before advancing to the next.
Delay advanced AI features until core data capture and descriptive analytics are stable.
frameworks.when_to_use: When building an AI-enabled advisory or analytics product that must deliver value quickly while reducing delivery risk.
failure_modes: Trying to implement all capabilities at once.
Adding RAG or profiling before data ingestion and basic analytics are reliable.
Lack of explicit validation gates between phases.

frameworks.name: Comparative architecture synthesis
frameworks.definition: A decision framework that compares two candidate solution designs against user objectives, isolates strengths and weaknesses, and produces a consolidated target architecture optimized for simplicity, robustness, and development ease.
steps: Map both proposals to the original objectives.
Compare each architecture across simplicity, robustness, performance, and evolvability.
Identify where one proposal outperforms the other for specific use cases.
Synthesize a final design that keeps the best elements and removes unnecessary complexity.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an architecture needs to be selected or refined from multiple competing drafts.
failure_modes: Optimizing for technical sophistication rather than user objectives.
Retaining redundant components from both designs.
Failing to reconcile conflicting stack choices into one coherent solution.

playbooks.title: Translate a Markdown specification into a coding-AI build prompt

playbooks.trigger: A deduplication script is missing duplicates or behaving inconsistently across repeated runs.

Separate URL-based duplicates from title-based fallbacks.

frameworks.name: Bid O&M hit-point analysis
frameworks.definition: A structured method for identifying the client’s evaluation priorities, the operational risks of the assignment, and the specific response angles that should be emphasised in the organisation and methodology section of a technical proposal.
steps: Map the assignment objective, institutional setting, and delivery sequence.
Identify evaluation-sensitive themes such as relevance, feasibility, coordination, governance, and monitoring.
Translate those themes into explicit bid messages, methods, and safeguards.
Check consistency between the proposed approach, team design, and resource planning.
Prioritise the most persuasive elements and eliminate generic narrative.
frameworks.when_to_use: When preparing a technical proposal for a complex advisory assignment where the organisation and methodology must demonstrate both understanding of the task and confidence in delivery.
failure_modes: Overly generic bid language that does not reflect the specific assignment.

Weak linkage between risks, mitigation measures, and staffing choices.
Failure to distinguish the proposal from standard consulting boilerplate.

Describe the resource plan in terms of roles, sequencing, level of effort, and decision points, making the staffing logic visible.
State the main risks and explain how the methodology reduces them, without sounding defensive or abstract.
Conclude by tying the approach back to successful delivery, institutional trust, and value for money.
playbooks.applicable_when: Applicable for senior advisory teams writing the methodology section of a bid for a public or IFI-funded infrastructure, transport, or technical assistance assignment.

frameworks.name: Three-Lens Road Underinvestment Assessment
frameworks.definition: Evaluate road underinvestment through three complementary lenses: cost, risk, and performance, then synthesize their combined effect on condition, safety, reliability, and resilience.
steps: Establish the baseline condition and service profile of the road network.
Quantify direct and indirect costs attributable to underinvestment.
Assess safety and resilience risks under current and future stressors.
Measure performance impacts such as reliability, accessibility, and delay.
Integrate findings to identify priority intervention areas and consequences of inaction.
frameworks.when_to_use: When advising on the strategic consequences of deferred road maintenance or underinvestment in a national network.
failure_modes: Treating the analysis as a pure engineering condition review and ignoring economic effects.
Measuring impacts without linking them to a baseline or counterfactual investment scenario.
Overweighting visible defects while missing systemwide reliability and resilience losses.

playbooks.title: Structure a national road underinvestment assessment for a client audience

Identify the data needed for each strand and note gaps explicitly.
Compare current performance against a counterfactual investment or maintenance path.
Translate technical findings into cost, risk, and service implications for decision-makers.
Conclude with priority actions and the implications of delaying investment.

frameworks.definition: A structured advisory method to assess a tolling strategy, refine its policy and commercial logic, and convert it into an implementation roadmap.

Assess network suitability, prioritizing candidate road sections using supply, demand, affordability, and revenue logic.
Review tariff policy, user segmentation, and equity implications.
Evaluate tolling technology and operating model options at a strategic level.
Translate findings into phased implementation, governance, risk, and monitoring plans.

failure_modes: Treating the strategy as a technical design exercise instead of a policy-commercial one.

Producing an implementation plan without governance, phasing, and risk controls.

Map major contractors, subcontractors, and material suppliers.
Compare bid patterns across projects and geographies.

frameworks.name: Infrastructure Packaging and Contracting Decision Framework

frameworks.name: ToR-to-Scoring Alignment Framework
frameworks.definition: A proposal-writing method that maps each evaluation criterion to the specific evidence, narrative, and deliverable language needed to earn marks.

Translate that capability into the exact output or approach promised in the bid.
Use precise examples that show how the team will deliver in practice.

failure_modes: Asserting expertise without evidence.
Using examples that are too broad or unrelated to the assignment.

For each scored item, add evidence of understanding, method, and delivery realism.
Tailor the team description to the assignment's geography, language, and technical needs.
Test whether each section reads like a convincing answer to an evaluator, not a generic capability statement.
playbooks.applicable_when: When bidding for development, infrastructure, or policy advisory contracts where evaluation criteria are explicit and scoring is weighted.

frameworks.name: Diagnóstico de concesión heredada y opciones de transición
frameworks.definition: Marco para analizar una concesión de transporte existente y determinar cómo condiciona, pero no predetermina, los modelos futuros de gestión de una ampliación.
steps: Delimitar el régimen contractual vigente y sus obligaciones esenciales.
Identificar qué aspectos de la concesión actual condicionan la ampliación: uso de infraestructura, continuidad operativa y coordinación de sistemas.
Comparar familias de salida: nuevo contrato público, modelo público-privado o gestión pública.
Traducir cada opción en trámites, hitos administrativos y consecuencias jurídicas.
Dejar el análisis económico-financiero para fases posteriores, limitándose en Fase 1 a las implicaciones estructurales.
frameworks.when_to_use: Cuando existe una concesión en servicio y el nuevo proyecto debe estudiar alternativas sin asumir que la ampliación se integrará por modificación del contrato existente.
failure_modes: Partir de la premisa de que la concesión actual debe ampliarse por defecto.
Mezclar en Fase 1 conclusiones financieras que aún no están soportadas por datos.
Reducir el análisis a un mero resumen contractual sin valorar opciones institucionales distintas.

playbooks.title: Redactar el alcance jurídico-administrativo de Fase 1 para una ampliación de metro
playbooks.trigger: Cuando hay que describir, en una oferta o informe, cómo se analizará la gestión actual y qué opciones futuras se dejarán preparadas sin sobredimensionar el trabajo.
steps: Explicar que el objetivo es entender la concesión actual como punto de partida, no como solución predeterminada.
Describir la revisión documental del contrato vigente y de los elementos que afectan a la futura ampliación.
Precisar que se estudiarán alternativas de gestión y explotación de la red ampliada, con especial atención a la articulación administrativa y jurídica.
Subrayar que en esta fase solo se sentarán bases para el análisis posterior, sin cuantificar todavía la viabilidad económico-financiera de las opciones.
Cerrar con una formulación prudente que muestre conocimiento técnico sin comprometer trabajos innecesarios.
playbooks.applicable_when: Útil en pliegos, memorias técnicas y respuestas a cliente donde conviene demostrar criterio sin prometer más de lo exigido.

frameworks.name: Marco de entrada al mercado ferroviario de mercancías en España

Comprobar el cumplimiento continuado de normas técnicas, laborales y de seguridad.

frameworks.name: Lente de due diligence para un plan de negocio ferroviario
frameworks.definition: Revisión estructurada de hipótesis de inversión, ingresos, competencia y opex para validar la credibilidad económica de un proyecto ferroviario.
steps: Contrastar las hipótesis de inversión con costes reales de material rodante y demás activos necesarios.
Revisar la demanda potencial del corredor y la lógica de tarifas e ingresos.
Construir escenarios de competencia y sustitución con otras autopistas ferroviarias, marítimas y combinaciones logísticas.
Desglosar el opex por cánones, terminales, energía, personal, mantenimiento y otros costes.
Identificar supuestos frágiles, duplicidades y riesgos de subestimación o sobreestimación.
frameworks.when_to_use: Cuando se revisa un business plan ferroviario de un nuevo operador y el presupuesto obliga a priorizar las hipótesis que más mueven la viabilidad.
failure_modes: Tratar el plan como una suma de cifras sin revisar coherencia operativa.
Ignorar escenarios competitivos y efectos de canibalización o sustitución.
Dejar el opex demasiado agregado y perder sensibilidad sobre los grandes drivers de coste.

playbooks.title: Revisar un plan de negocio ferroviario con presupuesto limitado
playbooks.trigger: El cliente pide una due diligence ligera de un proyecto de mercancías por ferrocarril y no hay tiempo ni presupuesto para un análisis exhaustivo.
steps: Priorizar las hipótesis que más afectan a la viabilidad: inversión, demanda, tarifas y opex.
Contrastar cada supuesto con fuentes normativas, prácticas de mercado y comparables operativos.
Separar lo que es obligatorio de lo que es una hipótesis comercial del promotor.
Modelizar escenarios base, prudente y adverso para captar sensibilidad.
Cerrar con un listado corto de riesgos críticos, supuestos a validar y decisiones pendientes.

Map financing sources against asset ownership.
Assign delivery responsibility for civil works, systems, rolling stock, and stations.

Identify which party bears ridership, construction, and refinancing risks.

Compare value-capture potential with project funding needs.

Define the role of central, regional, and local government in approvals, guarantees, and supervision.
Translate the preferred model into a study scope that a technical advisor can credibly deliver.

frameworks.name: PPP risk allocation lens

Test on representative threads before applying to the whole corpus.
frameworks.when_to_use: When the email body contains long reply-all chains with repeated names and signatures that obscure the discussion structure.

playbooks.title: Negotiate an IE liability cap with a financing sponsor
playbooks.trigger: An independent engineer is being asked to rely on its reports/certificates for lender drawdowns and wants to limit aggregate exposure to its fees.

Check whether the draft makes the IE responsible for borrower reliance or project outcomes beyond professional diligence.
Propose an express aggregate liability cap tied to fees and state it applies to all claims, including reliance-based claims.
Preserve standard carve-outs only if unavoidable and narrowly defined.
Provide a short business rationale showing the cap is needed to keep insurance and pricing aligned with the scope of services.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when a consultancy or independent engineer is asked to support financing decisions while keeping liability proportionate to fee income.

playbooks.title: AI-assisted resource extraction and tagging from message streams
playbooks.trigger: You need to turn a set of chat messages, links, and attachments into a clean list of useful resources for later review or publication.
steps: Extract URLs, attachments, and embedded links from each message.
Remove obvious noise and internal-navigation links using predefined exclusion patterns.
Normalize surviving links to improve consistency and deduplication.
Infer a coarse resource type from extension or content hints.
Build a metadata record for each candidate resource, including context from the originating message.
Use an LLM to decide whether the candidate is actually valuable and, if so, to provide a name and short description.
Discard items judged non-valuable or too low-quality.
Repair weak titles with a second enrichment pass or simple human-readable fallbacks.
Assign a final category tag using a classifier.
Return the vetted resources as a structured JSON list.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when a non-technical user wants to explain or operationalize a human review workflow that cleans and classifies shared resources from chats or similar message feeds.

Reagrupar las mismas horas por experto y por estudio, dejando el resto como seguimiento o residual.

frameworks.name: Commercial separability framework for OE phases
frameworks.definition: A method to split owner’s engineer services into fixed-price and time-and-materials components based on autonomy, dependency on third-party inputs, and pricing uncertainty.
steps: Map each phase task to required inputs, decision dependencies, and deliverable maturity.
Classify tasks that can be completed independently once inputs are available as fixed-price candidates.
Classify tasks whose timing, volume, or rework depend on EPC submissions or client decisions as time-and-materials candidates.
Stress-test the split against realistic programme, interface risk, and procurement sequence.
Package the commercial proposal with clear assumptions, exclusions, and triggers for re-baselining.
frameworks.when_to_use: When preparing an advisory or engineering services proposal where part of the scope is defined but major dependencies remain outside the consultant’s control.
failure_modes: Over-fixing tasks that depend on third-party outputs.
Under-pricing the coordination and rework burden.
Ignoring sequencing risk between design review, EPC pricing, and negotiations.
Using a single pricing model for a mixed-autonomy scope.

playbooks.title: Clarify pricing risk before submitting an OE proposal
playbooks.trigger: The client has not yet provided the full feasibility study, but the team must price owner’s engineer services for phases with significant third-party dependencies.
steps: Identify which proposal elements rely on the feasibility study versus concept-level information already available.
Separate tasks that the consultant can execute independently from tasks contingent on EPC submissions, client decisions, or negotiation outcomes.
Draft targeted clarification questions to confirm current project status, information gaps, and procurement sequence.
Frame the commercial proposal so fixed-price items are limited to autonomous work and variable items are priced on a time-and-materials basis.
Summarise the residual risk created by missing inputs in executive language suitable for the client.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use in infrastructure-advisory bids where the consultant must submit a credible commercial offer despite incomplete design and procurement information.

playbooks.title: Prepare a client-ready strategy presentation from a complex OE proposal
playbooks.trigger: A long, technical proposal must be converted into a short executive slide deck for a non-technical client audience.
steps: Distil the proposal into 3–5 core messages: scope logic, risk allocation, programme realism, and commercial structure.
Translate technical dependencies into simple visuals and milestone-based sequencing.
Limit the slide count and keep the storyline focused on why the proposed delivery model reduces client risk.
Remove implementation detail that would distract from the commercial and governance message.
Ensure each slide has one clear takeaway that a senior client can absorb quickly.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when a bid team needs to present an advisory strategy to a public or private infrastructure client in a concise executive format.

frameworks.name: EPC+F value-for-money appraisal lens
frameworks.definition: A strategic advisory method to judge whether an EPC+F structure creates better value for the public client than conventional procurement, by comparing time, risk transfer, and lifecycle quality.
steps: Define the baseline: conventional public procurement with multilateral financing.
Compare delivery time and the economic value of earlier opening.
Assess construction-risk transfer to a capable contractor backed by financing and guarantees.
Compare imported-cost premium against durability, warranty, and quality uplift.
Summarize whether the package is justified for the state in strategic terms.
frameworks.when_to_use: When advising a public authority on whether an EPC+F proposal is worth pursuing versus a standard publicly financed route.
failure_modes: Turning it into a detailed financial model when only a high-level strategic appraisal is needed.
Ignoring baseline comparators and judging the proposal in isolation.
Overweighting headline construction cost and underweighting schedule and risk transfer.

playbooks.title: Shape a concise consultancy scope for an independent value-for-money study
playbooks.trigger: A sponsor wants a credible third-party study, but budget and duration are limited and the client needs a strategically focused output.
steps: State the policy question in one sentence: is EPC+F better value for the state than conventional procurement?
Limit the analysis to three pillars: time savings, construction-risk transfer, and quality/durability premium.
Define the comparator set using credible regional precedents and public sources.
Specify a level of depth suitable for a short, independent study rather than a full feasibility exercise.
Frame the deliverable as decision support for government, not as a definitive engineering estimate.
Use neutral language that increases credibility with a skeptical public client.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when preparing terms of reference, a proposal, or a workplan for a short advisory assignment intended to justify a non-standard delivery model.

frameworks.name: Dual-provider Claude access switch
frameworks.definition: A human-level workflow for alternating between a local model via proxy and Anthropic’s API without changing how you prompt.
steps: Use the local proxy only when you want offline or local-model behavior.
Use the proxy’s routing/configuration to point Claude Code at the local backend.
Keep a separate path for direct Anthropic usage when you want hosted-model quality or reliability.
Switch by changing the active provider configuration rather than changing prompts or workflows.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an advisor wants one Claude-based workflow that can flip between local inference and hosted API access.
failure_modes: Proxy is running but upstream model server is not reachable.
Configuration points to a provider that is disabled or missing a model.

playbooks.title: Iterative setup of Claude Code with a local Ollama backend
playbooks.trigger: You want to use Claude Code against a local Ollama model and need to troubleshoot it step by step.
steps: Start from a clean baseline and verify the local model server is running.
Confirm the proxy service is actually alive before testing Claude Code through it.
Check that the proxy configuration names an enabled provider and at least one model.
Test the Claude Code path with a simple prompt before adding switching logic.
If a request fails, distinguish whether the error comes from the proxy, the model server, or the provider route, then fix only that layer before moving on.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful when setting up an AI assistant workflow on a Mac and you want one confirmed step at a time rather than a full-firehose fix.

frameworks.name: EPC-vs-EPC+Maintenance Strategic Comparison
frameworks.definition: A consulting framework to compare an EPC-only offer with an integrated EPC-plus-maintenance model across market fit, economics, risk, and organisational readiness.
steps: Define the two target business models and scope boundaries.
Assess market demand, customer preferences, and competitor positioning.
Evaluate internal capabilities, resource needs, and operating model implications.
Compare revenue, margin, risk, and cash-flow impacts under scenarios.
Test legal, contractual, and governance implications.
Synthesize findings into a recommendation and implementation direction.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a business is deciding whether to expand from one-off EPC delivery into a longer-term maintenance-enabled offering.
failure_modes: Treating maintenance as a simple add-on rather than a different operating model.
Overweighting revenue upside and underestimating liability and service capability requirements.
Using purely financial metrics and ignoring strategic fit or customer trust.
Failing to separate implementation feasibility from commercial attractiveness.

frameworks.name: Value-at-Stake Business Model Appraisal
frameworks.definition: A structured method for quantifying the commercial upside and downside created by a proposed business model change, using revenue, profit, resource, and risk dimensions.
steps: Set a baseline for the current business model.
Estimate incremental order value from the new offer.
Estimate incremental profit from cost efficiencies or risk-premium capture.
Assess resource requirements, including profile mix, supplier costs, and delivery capacity.
Estimate effects on guarantees, warranties, and contractual exposures.
Compare scenarios and determine where value is created or destroyed.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a leadership team needs a quantified view of whether a more integrated offering is financially and operationally attractive.
failure_modes: Confusing revenue growth with value creation.
Leaving out hidden delivery resources or support costs.
Ignoring guarantee and warranty impacts.
Assuming risk premiums can be fully captured without customer pushback.

playbooks.title: Prepare a Business Strategy Memo for EPC Plus Maintenance
playbooks.trigger: Use when asked to draft a consultant-style narrative explaining how to analyse the strategic case for adding maintenance to an EPC offer.
steps: Frame the decision as a strategic choice between business models, not a product extension.
Separate the analysis into market, capability, financial, and risk lenses.
Write the qualitative argument around customer value, differentiation, and organisational fit.
Support the narrative with a parallel quantitative value-at-stake assessment.
Conclude with implications for go/no-go and next-step diligence.
playbooks.applicable_when: The audience is a non-technical business team that needs a clear, board-level narrative rather than an implementation plan.

playbooks.title: Design the Implementation Approach for an Integrated EPC-plus-Maintenance Offer
playbooks.trigger: Use when the preferred strategy has been selected and the team needs a high-level implementation storyline.
steps: Translate the chosen model into a phased project plan with governance and decision gates.
Identify partner and contractor sourcing needs.
Shape the target contract structure and liability principles.

Test which elements require stable commitment and which should remain adjustable over time.
Check whether risk-sharing is balanced or tilted toward government guarantees or operator protection.
Assess whether pricing can adapt to sustainability, technology, and demand changes without triggering repeated renegotiation.
Judge the framework against public objectives such as efficiency, safety, and decarbonisation.
frameworks.when_to_use: When reviewing or comparing concession models, tolling reforms, or road user charging policy from a public-private governance perspective.
failure_modes: Overly rigid contracts that cannot adapt to regulatory or technological change.

Allowing frequent ad hoc intervention that undermines credibility.

playbooks.title: Draft an executive response on RUC versus PPP viability
playbooks.trigger: A senior stakeholder asks whether national road user charging could threaten toll-road concessions or PPPs.
steps: Acknowledge the concern and separate short-term revenue effects from long-term network policy.
Explain that RUC and toll PPPs can coexist if they are designed for different purposes or road classes.
Note the real risks: overlap in charging, revenue substitution, and pressure on older concession models.
Emphasise that the policy question is not whether RUC exists, but how charging architecture, exemptions, and sequencing are designed.
Close by framing the issue as one of coherent system design rather than a zero-sum conflict.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for LinkedIn replies, conference Q&A, or client discussions about the future of tolling and concessions.

frameworks.name: CB/CV assembly from career evidence corpus
frameworks.definition: A human-led method to turn scattered career evidence into tailored CVs for proposals without manually rewriting the whole profile each time.
steps: Define the target CV archetype and proposal context.
Collect a bounded corpus of evidence: prior CVs, project docs, emails, and deliverables.
Tag evidence by project, role, sector, outcome, and seniority relevance.
Let an LLM draft candidate bullets and summaries from the tagged evidence.
Review, prune, and adapt the output to the specific opportunity and Word template.
frameworks.when_to_use: When you repeatedly need proposal-specific CVs and have dispersed career evidence across emails, documents, and prior CVs.
failure_modes: Trying to process everything at once and losing relevance.
Using the LLM as a substitute for judgement, causing generic or inflated CV text.
Skipping evidence tagging, which makes later reuse difficult.
Over-automating before defining the target CV format and use-case.

playbooks.title: Build a reusable CV evidence library for proposal-ready CBs
playbooks.trigger: You need to generate tailored CVs from a large, unstructured archive of career materials.
steps: Decide the main categories you will reuse across proposals, such as projects, roles, outcomes, and skills.
Gather source material from emails, project documents, presentations, and earlier CV versions.
Group material by project or client and keep only representative, high-value evidence.
Create a consistent way to label or summarise each item so it can be searched and reused later.
Use that curated evidence set as the input to an LLM when drafting a proposal-specific CV.
Review each generated CV to ensure it matches the opportunity and does not include irrelevant material.
playbooks.applicable_when: You have lots of career documentation in multiple places and want a repeatable way to produce tailored, credible CVs.

playbooks.title: Use an LLM to draft a Word-based CV from structured career notes
playbooks.trigger: You already have career notes or extracted text and want the model to populate a predefined Word CV format.
steps: Prepare the career content in a way the model can read consistently, with sections such as experience, achievements, and skills.
Ask the LLM to convert that content into a format aligned with your target CV sections.
Map the generated content to the corresponding parts of your Word template.
Review the draft for accuracy, tone, and relevance to the specific proposal.
Iterate by tightening the prompt or source notes if the result is too broad or too generic.
playbooks.applicable_when: You have a fixed CV template and want faster drafting while keeping human review in the loop.

frameworks.name: Utility-by-task-complexity lens
frameworks.definition: Assess Copilot by separating routine, semi-structured, and high-judgment tasks, then judge where it adds real leverage versus where expert human work still dominates.
steps: List the main task families in your role.
Classify each one by complexity and judgment intensity.
Test Copilot against each family, not against the role as a whole.
Summarize where it helps, where it stalls, and why that matters for senior work.
frameworks.when_to_use: When explaining GenAI value to a senior non-technical audience in a professional role with mixed task types.
failure_modes: Becoming too generic and ignoring the difference between routine and strategic work.
Turning the assessment into a vendor feature review instead of a work-value analysis.
Overstating usefulness in advanced advisory tasks.

playbooks.title: Present a concise personal assessment of Copilot in a senior advisory role
playbooks.trigger: You need to explain, in a few minutes, whether Copilot is genuinely useful for your own high-level work.
steps: State your role and why your expectations were high.
Say you tested Copilot in daily Office workflows over a short period.
Separate what it does adequately from what it fails to do in sophisticated advisory tasks.
Use one concrete example of a failed attempt to show the boundary of current capability.
Close with a balanced takeaway: useful as support, not yet a substitute for senior judgment.
playbooks.applicable_when: You are speaking to peers, clients, or internal stakeholders about GenAI adoption from a leadership perspective.

frameworks.name: No-cost extension leverage check
frameworks.definition: A practical advisory lens for deciding whether to press for, resist, or condition an extension request by testing who caused delay, who benefits, and what the contract allows.
steps: Identify the contractual trigger for an extension.
Assess whether delay is attributable to the contractor or the client.
Check whether required approvals or committee validation are prerequisites or parallel activities.
Map leverage points: performance, notice, deemed approval, and amendment rights.
Decide whether to request, accept, reject, or condition the extension.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a client or contracting authority proposes a no-cost extension and the contractor wants to understand exposure, leverage, and negotiation posture.
failure_modes: Treating every delay as grounds for extension.
Ignoring deemed-approval or notice mechanisms.
Conceding an extension without linking it to scope, time, or liability adjustments.

frameworks.name: Consortium default containment
frameworks.definition: A governance approach for a JV leader to contain the impact of one member’s delay or underperformance while preserving project delivery and contractual position.
steps: Confirm the delayed member’s contractual obligations and the specific missed outputs.
Document repeated delay, resource shortfalls, and communications.
Issue a formal notice requiring cure or assurance of resources.
Escalate to the JV governance body for reallocation or mitigation measures.
Reassign work or backfill resources if cure fails, while reserving rights against the defaulting member.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a consortium or JV member is late, under-resourced, or likely to miss final deliverables close to contract end.
failure_modes: Waiting until the end date to act.
Informal pressure without written notice.
Reassigning work without governance approval or a documented basis.

playbooks.title: Assess a consortium member’s resource risk before contract close-out
playbooks.trigger: A JV member is late on deliverables and may not be able to mobilize the people or capacity needed to finish.
steps: Separate output delay from future capacity risk.
Ask for a written assurance of remaining resource availability.
Review the member’s delivery history and any prior warnings.
Prepare contingency resources from the other JV members.
Escalate internally if assurance is weak or absent.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use in the final phase of a project where one consortium member’s staffing or capacity threatens completion.

frameworks.name: Concession Scope Decomposition
frameworks.definition: A consulting method for separating an infrastructure concession into asset coverage, operating obligations, commercial rights, and interface risks.
steps: Identify the assets included in the concession and any ancillary links or bypasses.
Separate construction, operation, maintenance, and toll-exploitation obligations.
Note any distinct subsidiaries or operating entities involved.
Flag special interface items such as spurs, bypasses, or shared O&M arrangements.
frameworks.when_to_use: When summarising a toll-road or transport concession for an advisory, investor, or management audience.
failure_modes: Confusing the legal concession scope with the current operating business description.
Omitting included sub-assets such as bypasses or spurs.
Blurring ownership, concessionaire, and operator roles.

frameworks.name: Concession Risk Comparison Lens
frameworks.definition: A structured way to compare two concessions by requirements, relative risk, external benchmark, and mitigations.
steps: Summarise the main technical or operational requirements for each concession.
Compare where one concession is stricter or more lenient than the other.
Assess the relative risk level arising from those differences.
Benchmark against a third reference set or peer concession model.
Translate the differences into practical mitigation actions.
frameworks.when_to_use: When turning a detailed contract or slide deck into an executive summary focused on risk and actions.
failure_modes: Producing a feature list without a judgement on relative risk.
Missing the benchmark that explains why one concession looks worse than another.
Stopping at diagnosis without proposing mitigations.

playbooks.title: Prepare a One-Slide Executive Summary of a Concession Assessment
playbooks.trigger: You need to compress a multi-dimensional concession review into a single board- or client-ready slide.
steps: Group the message into three blocks: requirements, risk, and mitigation.
Use a side-by-side comparison for the concessions being assessed.
Keep wording short and use visual hierarchy to show the main difference first.
Add one line on the external benchmark only if it materially changes the interpretation.
End with 2–3 actions that management can take.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for senior advisory presentations where clarity and visual economy matter more than detail.

playbooks.title: Frame an Upcoming Regulatory or Technical Change as a Concession Risk
playbooks.trigger: You need a short slide text explaining why an announced or expected standard change matters to an operating concession.
steps: State the current operating framework.
Describe the direction of travel in the new standard at a high level.
Explain why the concession is exposed, using plain business language.
Avoid claiming certainty on timing or mechanics if the source is still informal.
Link the change to possible commercial or contractual consequences.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful when briefing non-technical stakeholders on an emerging policy or standards shift.

playbooks.title: Lender-facing EPC replaceability assessment

frameworks.name: Hub-and-spoke digital coordination model
frameworks.definition: A governance model that coordinates digital capabilities across autonomous business units through shared standards, reusable assets, and a small central orchestration layer, without full operational centralization.
steps: Map existing digital capabilities by unit and identify overlaps, gaps, and critical shared needs.
Define a small set of group-wide standards for data, tooling, security, and delivery.
Create a central coordination forum to prioritize cross-unit initiatives and resolve conflicts.
Keep execution in business units or specialist subsidiaries, using shared assets where beneficial.
Track adoption, reuse, and business impact through a common portfolio view.
frameworks.when_to_use: When digital capabilities are dispersed across subsidiaries or divisions and the goal is to capture synergies without dismantling local autonomy.
failure_modes: Becomes de facto centralization and loses business-unit ownership.
Creates standards with no adoption mechanism.
Over-focuses on governance and under-invests in reusable assets.
Fails to define which decisions are made centrally versus locally.

frameworks.name: Capability-led digital portfolio prioritization
frameworks.definition: A method for selecting digital initiatives by linking them to existing enterprise capabilities, market differentiation, and measurable operational value rather than by technology enthusiasm alone.
steps: Inventory current digital capabilities and the business problems they already solve.
Identify market trends and client demands that could amplify those capabilities.
Rank initiatives by strategic fit, scalability, and reusability across projects or geographies.
Select a small number of lighthouse use cases that demonstrate value quickly.
Use the pilots to refine the operating model and decide what to scale.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a professional-services firm has pockets of digital strength but needs a disciplined way to decide what to scale group-wide.
failure_modes: Picks the most novel technology instead of the most valuable use case.
Scatters investment across too many pilots.
Ignores implementation readiness and change management.
Cannot translate pilots into repeatable offerings or internal productivity gains.

playbooks.title: Design a common data platform for a multi-entity engineering group
playbooks.trigger: The group uses document repositories and office suites widely, but leadership wants a shared data foundation for projects, operations, and analytics.
steps: Start by distinguishing documents from data: identify the structured and semi-structured information that should be reusable across projects and entities.
Define the common data domains that matter most, such as projects, assets, inspections, costs, risk, and performance.
Set a target architecture in plain language: sources feed a governed data layer, which then supports reporting, analytics, and AI use cases.
Decide which capabilities stay in specialist tools and which must be exposed through the common layer.
Establish ownership for data quality, metadata, access rights, and usage rules.
Prioritize one or two high-value use cases to prove the platform’s value before broad rollout.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful when leadership suspects that a document repository is not enough and needs a true enterprise data foundation for decision-making and reuse.

playbooks.title: Structure a digital leadership role for a federated professional-services firm
playbooks.trigger: A firm needs someone to coordinate digital transformation across autonomous subsidiaries, technical units, and territories without becoming a pure IT function.
steps: Define the mandate around business outcomes, not systems administration.
Give the role authority to set standards, convene stakeholders, and arbitrate priorities.
Make the role responsible for portfolio selection, not day-to-day delivery of every initiative.
Require strong fluency in both technology trends and consulting economics.
Ensure the person can translate between technical teams, business leaders, and external clients.
Tie success to adoption, reuse, and measurable value creation across the group.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful when the organization has fragmented digital capability and needs an enterprise-level leader who can orchestrate, align, and scale.

frameworks.name: Contract-to-Opportunity Mapping
frameworks.definition: A consulting method that translates concession obligations into revenue, cost, and risk levers for value engineering.
steps: Read the contract obligations by workstream: design, construction, operations, maintenance, tolling.
Identify what is mandatory versus optional or flexible within the technical provisions.
Map each obligation to a potential commercial or operational lever: capacity, connectivity, cost, revenue, or risk.
Prioritise opportunities that improve traffic performance without increasing contractual exposure.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a concession has been awarded and the client wants advisory support to improve the scheme within contractual constraints.
failure_modes: Treating the preliminary design as fixed when the contract may allow optimisation.
Focusing only on capex savings and missing revenue or penalty impacts.
Ignoring how value engineering changes may alter operational risk or compensation exposure.

playbooks.title: Brief Directors on a Post-Award Value Engineering Opportunity

List the disciplines required: traffic engineering, roadway design, tolling systems, O&M, and contract/risk analysis.

playbooks.title: 5-Year DBFO Hand-Back Value-Protection Workflow
playbooks.trigger: A road DBFO concession is entering the final hand-back preparation window and the concessionaire wants to reduce unnecessary renewal spend while preserving compliance and relationships.
steps: Review hand-back obligations, residual-life requirements, and any inspection/testing standards in the contract.

Prioritise interventions by safety, contractual exposure, and residual-life risk rather than by blanket renewal.
Use lifecycle-cost reasoning to choose the least-cost intervention that still meets hand-back standards.
Run regular alignment meetings with the grantor to agree scope, timing, evidence, and dispute-avoidance steps.
Maintain a complete hand-back dossier with condition evidence, works history, assumptions, and outstanding risks.
Prepare escalation and mediation paths early for any disagreement on scope or condition.

Merge overlapping descriptions into one concise project narrative.

frameworks.name: Knowledge-Architecture-by-Category
frameworks.definition: A way to organize custom-GPT knowledge around document types and use cases rather than listing every file individually.
steps: Group source materials into a small number of functional categories.
Identify what each category is meant to support in GPT responses.
Prioritize canonical, stable documents over exhaustive inventories.
Keep the instruction prompt focused on how to use the knowledge, not on file enumeration.
Refresh the knowledge set when source documents change materially.
frameworks.when_to_use: When designing a custom GPT for a consulting or advisory workflow that relies on uploaded reference documents.
failure_modes: Uploading too many overlapping documents and creating ambiguity.
Trying to maintain a full document list inside instructions.
Mixing outdated drafts with final reference documents.
Failing to label which sources are authoritative versus illustrative.

frameworks.name: Public-Repository-Reference-Model
frameworks.definition: A method for using publicly accessible repositories or shared document locations as an external source of truth, while keeping the GPT instructions simple and source-aware.
steps: Define which repository or portal is the authoritative source.
Ensure documents are publicly accessible or otherwise reachable under the chosen setup.
Instruct the GPT to refer to the repository conceptually rather than rely on a fixed internal document list.
Use stable document naming and versioning conventions.
Periodically verify that links and access permissions still work.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a consulting team wants a custom GPT to stay aligned with an external document set that changes over time.
failure_modes: Assuming the GPT can freely browse any repository without access constraints.
Letting document links drift or expire.
Using poorly controlled shared folders with multiple conflicting versions.
Expecting the GPT to know documents that were not actually accessible during setup.

playbooks.title: Design a Custom GPT for Consulting Deliverables
playbooks.trigger: You want a subject-specific GPT that helps a consulting firm produce better outputs for a defined contract or advisory task.
steps: Clarify the GPT’s audience and primary use cases.
Define the core outputs it should help with, such as drafting, summarizing, comparing, or quality-checking.
Select the most important knowledge categories rather than enumerating every document.
Write instructions in plain language suitable for a non-IT end user.
Specify how the GPT should handle uncertainty, missing information, and conflicts among sources.
Test against realistic user questions and refine the instruction set.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for non-technical professionals creating a custom GPT to support consulting work and stakeholder-facing deliverables.

playbooks.title: Use External Public Sources as GPT Reference Material
playbooks.trigger: You want a custom GPT to work from publicly accessible repositories or shared document systems instead of only uploaded files.
steps: Identify the external source that should act as the canonical reference.
Check that the source is stable, accessible, and organized.
Decide whether the GPT should summarize, cite, or merely consult that source conceptually.
Document the boundaries of what the GPT can and cannot rely on.
Create a fallback rule for cases where the external source is unavailable or ambiguous.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful when knowledge changes frequently and maintaining a static upload set would be inefficient.

frameworks.name: Prompt-to-Task Framing
frameworks.definition: Adapt the prompt to the intended business output, using role, task, and constraints to get more relevant GenAI responses.
steps: State the intended deliverable clearly.
Specify the business context and audience.
Add constraints that narrow the output to the use case.
Iterate by refining the prompt when the first answer is too generic.
frameworks.when_to_use: When asking an LLM to produce a specific advisory artifact rather than a general explanation.
failure_modes: Too vague prompts produce generic outputs.
Overloading the prompt with unrelated details reduces focus.
The model may still miss domain nuance without examples or context.

frameworks.name: Few-shot Prompting for Niche Vocabulary
frameworks.definition: Teach an LLM unfamiliar terminology by giving one or more examples that pair definition and usage.
steps: Define the unfamiliar term plainly.
Provide an example sentence or usage pattern.
Add another example if needed to reinforce the pattern.
Ask the model to imitate the example in the target task.
frameworks.when_to_use: When working in a narrow field where the model may not know specialist vocabulary or phrasing.
failure_modes: Examples that are ambiguous or weak lead to poor imitation.
Too few examples may not generalize.
The model may copy surface form without understanding the intended meaning.

playbooks.title: Use GenAI to test a narrow professional task with better prompting

Provide one or two concrete examples of the kind of answer needed.
Refine the prompt until the response matches the intended use case.

steps: Read the administrative and technical specifications together as a single risk-allocation package.
Map each risk topic to explicit clauses, exclusions, and remedies.
Distinguish contractual allocation from statutory fallback rules.
Test whether the concessionaire can pass through risks and remedies to subcontractors or operators.
Summarise the practical consequences for pricing, financing, and claims management.
frameworks.when_to_use: When advising on a public concession or project-finance transaction and the key question is who bears a specific project risk.
failure_modes: Treating one pliego in isolation and missing cross-references.
Confusing theoretical legal allocation with the actual contractual wording.
Overstating pass-throughability to subcontractors without checking back-to-back limits.
Ignoring remedies, caps, and termination triggers that change the economic allocation.

playbooks.title: Draft a lender-facing worst-case liability-cap analysis for an O&M subcontract

steps: Identify the contractually relevant failure modes during operation and maintenance.
Build a severe-but-plausible replacement scenario, including penalties, replacement costs, recovery works, and uplift in maintenance spend.
Add timing variants for years with major maintenance and other critical periods.
Compare each scenario’s incremental cost against the subcontractor’s liability cap.
Translate the result into lender-facing conclusions on whether the cap is likely to be exceeded.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when a concessionaire has back-to-back O&M arrangements and the lender wants a robustness test rather than a legal memo.

playbooks.title: Prepare a concise concession-contract memo for a non-technical audience

steps: Restate the question in commercial terms.
Check the concession documents for the relevant clause hierarchy and any statutory overlay.
Extract only the operative rule, threshold, or consequence.
Explain the practical impact on risk, price, delay, or termination.
Keep the answer concise and tie it back to the concession structure.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when responding to advisory questions on Spanish concession contracts where the audience wants a technically sound but succinct answer.

failure_modes: Over-weighting global best practice that is not transferable to African road agencies.
Treating CVA as a purely technical exercise and missing governance or asset-management implications.
Producing a literature review that is too broad to guide practical adoption.

playbooks.title: Build an Africa-Relevant State of the Art on Road Climate Vulnerability
playbooks.trigger: A team needs an updated research synthesis on climate vulnerability assessments in transport and roads, with explicit relevance to Africa and recent literature.
steps: Set the review lens to global evidence, but retain only lessons that can inform African road resilience policy and practice.
Prioritise the last two years of literature, while keeping a maximum five-year window for context.
Separate transport-sector findings from road-sector findings, then identify overlaps and road-specific implications.
Integrate the latest World Bank publication as a central reference point and use it to update the analytical narrative.
Draft outputs in a form that can feed policy papers, guidelines, and resilience-mainstreaming recommendations.

playbooks.title: Configure GitHub branch rulesets to require pull-request approval
playbooks.trigger: You want to enforce PR approvals on a private GitHub repository with a free account.
steps: Open the repository settings in GitHub.
Go to the branch protection or rulesets area.
Create a ruleset targeting the branch you want to protect, such as main.
Enable the rule that requires a pull request before merging.
Set the required number of approving reviews.
Optionally require Code Owners review, dismiss stale approvals, and include administrators.
Save and enable the ruleset.
playbooks.applicable_when: Use when you need a human review gate before changes can be merged into a protected branch.

playbooks.title: Diagnose and stop a lingering Streamlit background process on macOS
playbooks.trigger: A Streamlit app seems to keep running after VS Code is closed, and the user wants to prevent it in future.
steps: Confirm whether a real Streamlit process is running rather than the grep command itself.
Look for the process in Activity Monitor or by checking the process list.
If it is running, stop it from the terminal or Activity Monitor before closing VS Code.
Avoid detaching the app with background execution patterns during development.
If needed, review startup or automation mechanisms that may be launching the app independently.
playbooks.applicable_when: When a locally run Streamlit app appears to persist after an IDE is closed, especially on macOS.

claims.text: `~/.zshrc` is a configuration file read by Zsh at shell startup, not something you normally execute directly.
claims.source_excerpt: ~/.zshrc is not an executable script you run directly. It's a configuration file that Zsh automatically reads and executes when you start a new terminal session.

claims.text: To apply changes made in `.zshrc` without restarting the terminal, you can source the file in the current shell.
claims.source_excerpt: If you've made changes to `.zshrc` and want to apply them without restarting the terminal: `source ~/.zshrc`

claims.text: A Streamlit app started as a normal server process will keep running until it is explicitly stopped, so closing VS Code alone does not terminate it.
claims.source_excerpt: it starts a persistent server. Just closing VS Code doesn't stop it.

claims.text: The `grep streamlit` line in `ps aux | grep streamlit` is usually the grep command itself, not a real Streamlit app process.
claims.source_excerpt: This is just the `grep streamlit` command itself, which runs momentarily while searching for “streamlit” in the process list.

glossary.one_line: The Zsh startup configuration file for interactive shell settings and commands.

A Python framework for building interactive data apps that runs a local web server.
macOS utility for viewing and managing running processes.
A process identifier used to refer to a specific running program.
A process that keeps running after its parent session or app closes.

playbooks.title: Iterative transcription-spec refinement

steps: Start with the baseline transcription task and clarify the target languages.
Confirm the desired output destination and file format.
Refine the transcript structure from line-by-line to paragraph-based output.

Preserve the earlier requirements while updating only the requested formatting and interaction behavior.

frameworks.name: CRM ligero por fases para una organización relacional
frameworks.definition: Método para definir un CRM mínimo viable en una empresa tradicional, priorizando visibilidad básica, adopción gradual y reducción de fricciones antes de añadir automatización o analítica avanzada.
steps: Delimitar los usuarios objetivo y los pocos datos realmente imprescindibles.

Reservar capacidades avanzadas para cuando el uso básico esté interiorizado.

frameworks.name: Phased external-scope carve-out for advisory bids
frameworks.definition: A method for isolating only the consultant work that genuinely belongs outside the prime contractor’s scope, then aligning deliverables and effort to the prime contract phases.
steps: Identify the exact phase and workstream boundaries in the main RfP.
Exclude all activities the prime contractor will perform internally.
Retain only the external consultant’s niche inputs that feed broader deliverables.
Condense outputs into a small number of aligned deliverables.
Check effort assumptions against the expected team size and study maturity.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an advisory firm needs to subcontract only a narrow analytical component of a larger infrastructure or feasibility study.
failure_modes: Over-scoping the subcontractor into prime-contractor responsibilities.
Creating deliverables that do not map cleanly to the main contract.
Inflating the team beyond what the task actually requires.

Keep deliverables few and explicitly linked to the parent Phase 1 outputs.
Estimate a small, conservative team and level of effort consistent with the narrow scope.
